stem: A cylinder is rolling over a rough surface. Then it enters a smooth region. What will happen to its translational and rotational K.E.? (Figure: cylinder with centre velocity v 0 and spin ω 0 crossing from a “Rough” strip onto a “Smooth” strip.) —

Three particles are fixed on a ring rolling on the ground as shown in the figure. Find the kinetic energy of the system. (Ring of mass 4m and radius R rolls without slipping with centre speed v; a particle m is fixed at each end of the horizontal diameter and a particle 2m is fixed at the lowest point of the ring.) —

In the figure shown, a small ball of mass m can move without sliding in a fixed semicircular track of radius R in a vertical plane. It is released from the top. Find the resultant force on the wall at the lowest point of the track. —

A disc of mass m is rolling on the ground as shown in the figure. Find the angular momentum of the disc w.r.t. point O on the ground. (The disc has radius R, its centre moves with velocity v to the right, and it spins anticlockwise with ω = v/2R; O is the point of the ground directly below the disc.) —

A block is suspended by a string wound around a cylinder of radius 15 cm, which can rotate freely about its fixed axis. If the angular speed of the cylinder at a certain instant is 8 rad/s, find the speed of the descending block at that instant. —

key: k²/R² = 1 → a ring or a hollow cylinder
stem: Starting from rest, an object rolls down along an incline that rises by 3 in every 5 (along it). The object gains a speed of √10 m/s as it travels a distance of 5/3 m along the incline. What can be the possible shape/s of the object? — (Level: Board)
A body is rolling without slipping on a horizontal surface and its rotational kinetic energy is equal to the translational kinetic energy. The body is (a) Disc (b) Sphere (c) Cylinder (d) Ring —

A solid sphere of mass M and radius R is placed on top of a rough inclined surface of height h. It rolls down the incline without slipping. Its kinetic energy on reaching the bottom of the incline will be: (a) Mgh (b) Less than Mgh as the surface is rough (c) More than Mgh because of additional rotational kinetic energy (d) Depending on the coefficient of static friction between the sphere and the surface. —

For a hollow cylinder and a solid cylinder rolling without slipping on an inclined plane, then which of these reaches earlier on the ground? (a) Solid cylinder (b) Hollow cylinder (c) Both simultaneously (d) Can't say anything —

A disc is rolling, the velocity of its centre of mass is V cm . Then which one will be correct? (a) The velocity of highest point is 2V cm and point of contact is zero (b) The velocity of highest point is √(4gh/3) and point of contact is V cm (c) The velocity of highest point is 2V cm and point of contact is V cm (d) The velocity of highest point is 2V cm and point of contact is 2V cm —

A solid cylinder of mass M and radius R rolls without slipping down an inclined plane of length L and height h. What is the speed of its centre of mass when the cylinder reaches its bottom? (a) √(2gh) (b) √(3gh/4) (c) √(4gh/3) (d) √(4gh) —

A sphere of mass 0.5 kg and diameter 1 m rolls without sliding with a constant velocity of 5 m/s, calculate what is the ratio of the rotational K.E. to the total kinetic energy of the sphere. (a) 7/10 (b) 5/7 (c) 2/7 (d) 1/2 —

When a sphere of moment of inertia I about its centre of gravity and mass m rolls from rest down an inclined plane without slipping, its kinetic energy is (a) ½Iω² (b) ½mv² (c) Iω + mv (d) ½Iω² + ½mv² —

A thin hollow cylinder open at both ends : (i) Sliding without rolling (ii) Rolls without slipping, with the same speed. The ratio of kinetic energy in the two cases is (a) 1 : 1 (b) 4 : 1 (c) 1 : 2 (d) 2 : 1 —
A hollow sphere of diameter 0.2 m and mass 2 kg is rolling on an inclined plane with velocity υ = 0.5 m/s. The kinetic energy of the sphere is (a) 0.1 J (b) 0.3 J (c) 0.5 J (d) 0.42 J —
A spherical ball of mass 2 kg is rolling without slipping with a speed 4 m/s on a rough floor. Its rotational kinetic energy is : (a) 7.2 J (b) 6.4 J (c) 9.4 J (d) 11.6 J —
A ring and a disc having the same mass roll without slipping with the same linear velocity. If the kinetic energy of the ring is 8 J, then find the kinetic energy of the disc (in J). —

Consider a uniform solid cylinder of mass 21 g and radius 0.5 m rolling without slipping down an incline at inclination 30° with horizontal. Find the speed (in m/s) of COM of cylinder when it reaches the bottom. (Figure: a right triangle of height h = 0.3 m with the 30° angle at its base, the cylinder starting at the top.) —
A solid sphere of mass 2 kg rolls on a horizontal surface at 10 m/s and then rolls up an inclined plane of inclination 30°; find to which height (in m) it rolls? —

The total kinetic energy of a body of mass 10 kg and radius 0.5 m moving with a velocity of 2 m/s without slipping is 32.8 joule. The radius of gyration of the body is (a) 0.25 m (b) 0.2 m (c) 0.5 m (d) 0.4 m —

A particle moves along a circle of radius 20/π m with constant tangential acceleration. If the velocity of the particle is 80 m/s at the end of second revolution after motion has begun, then find the tangential acceleration (in m/s²). —

key: v C = mv/(M + m), along the particle's original direction
stem: Suppose the particle of the previous problem has a mass m and a speed v before the collision and it sticks to the rod after the collision. The rod has a mass M. Find the velocity of the centre of mass C of the system constituting “the rod plus the particle”. (The referred problem is Level-4 Q7 below: a uniform rod of length L lies on a smooth horizontal table and the particle strikes it perpendicularly at one end.) —

key: πL/12; and K is conserved exactly when M = 4m
stem: A uniform rod of length L lies on a smooth horizontal table. A particle moving on the table strikes the rod perpendicularly at an end and stops. Find the distance travelled by the centre of the rod by the time it turns through a right angle. Show that if the mass of the rod is four times that of the particle, the collision is elastic. —

A small sphere rolls down without slipping from the top of a track in a vertical plane. The track has an elevated section and a horizontal part. The horizontal part is 1 m above ground level and top of track is 2.4 m above the ground. Find the distance (in m) on the ground w.r.t. B where the sphere lands. (Figure: the curved track drops from A at 2.4 m to a horizontal ledge 1 m high whose edge is vertically above B.) —

Figure shows a hemisphere of radius 4R. A ball of radius R is released from position P. It rolls without slipping along the inner surface of the hemisphere. Linear speed of its centre of mass when the ball is at position Q, is: (a) √(30gR/7) (b) √(24gR/5) (c) √(40gR/9) (d) √(6gR) —

Two small balls A and B, each of mass m, are joined rigidly to the ends of a light rod of length L. The system translates on a frictionless horizontal surface with a velocity v 0 in a direction perpendicular to the rod. A particle P of mass m kept at rest on the surface sticks to the ball A as the ball collides with it. Find (a) the linear speeds of the balls A and B after the collision, (b) the velocity of the centre of mass C of the system A + B + P and (c) the angular speed of the system about C after the collision. [Hint : The light rod will exert a force on the ball B only along its length.] —
A sphere of mass m rolls on a plane surface. Find its kinetic energy at an instant when its centre moves with speed v. —

A plank P is placed on a solid cylinder S, which rolls on a horizontal surface. The two are of equal mass. There is no slipping at any of the surfaces in contact. The ratio of the kinetic energy of P to the kinetic energy of S is (a) 1 : 1 (b) 2 : 1 (c) 8 : 3 (d) 1 : 4 —

A reeled carpet of radius R is gently pushed. If it rolls without sliding and unreels, the speed of the centre of mass of the rolling portion when its radius is halved is (Neglect the vertical motion of the centre of mass) (a) √(7gR/3) (b) √(14gR/3) (c) √(8gR/3) (d) √(5gR/3) —
A sphere starts rolling down an incline of inclination θ. Find the speed of its centre when it has covered a distance l. —

A bucket is being lifted from a well using a rope wound around a cylindrical drum of radius 25 cm. The drum rotates about a fixed horizontal axis. At a certain instant, the drum has an angular speed of 8 rad/s. What is the linear speed of the bucket at that instant? (a) 1 m/s (b) 2 m/s (c) 4 m/s (d) 0.5 m/s —

A block hangs from a string wrapped on a disc of radius 20 cm free to rotate about its axis which is fixed in a horizontal position. If the angular speed of the disc is 10 rad/s at some instant, with what speed is the block going down at that instant? —

A uniform disc of radius R = 0.2 m kept over a rough horizontal surface is given velocity v 0 and angular velocity ω 0 . After some time its kinetic energy becomes zero. If v 0 = 10 m/s, find ω 0 . (Figure: the disc translates with v 0 to the right while ω 0 is a back-spin, opposite to the rolling sense.) (a) 50 rad/s (b) 100 rad/s (c) 150 rad/s (d) 200 rad/s —

A small disc is set rolling with a speed v on the horizontal part of the track of the previous problem from right to left. To what height will it climb up the curved part? (The track referred to is a horizontal stretch that curves smoothly upward at its left end; the disc rolls without slipping throughout.) —

Solve the previous problem if the friction coefficient between the 2.0 kg block and the plane below it is 0.5 and the plane below the 4.0 kg block is frictionless. (The problem referred to — carried over from the source text and answered 0.25 m/s² there — has a pulley of radius 10 cm and moment of inertia 0.5 kg m² at the apex of two 45° inclines, with a 4.0 kg block on one face and a 2.0 kg block on the other, joined by a light string that does not slip; find the acceleration of the 4.0 kg block.) —

Suppose the smaller pulley of the previous problem has its radius 5.0 cm and moment of inertia 0.10 kg-m². Find the tension in the part of the string joining the pulleys. (The problem referred to — carried over from the source text, where the small pulley was light and the answer was 0.89 m/s² — has a string wrapped on a wheel of moment of inertia 0.20 kg m² and radius 10 cm, led over the small pulley to support a hanging block of mass 2.0 kg.) —

A small spherical ball is released from a point at a height h on a rough track shown in figure. Assuming that it does not slip anywhere, find its linear speed when it rolls on the horizontal part of the track. (Figure: a curved ramp of height h flattening smoothly into a horizontal run.) —

A ring of mass m and radius R has three particles attached to the ring as shown in the figure. The centre of the ring has a speed v 0 . The kinetic energy of the system is (slipping is absent) (a) 6mv 0 ² (b) 12mv 0 ² (c) 4mv 0 ² (d) 8mv 0 ² (Figure: the ring rolls on the ground; a particle m sits at the topmost point, a particle m at the right-hand end of the horizontal diameter, and a particle 2m at the centre of the ring.) —

A uniform rod of mass m and length l is sliding between a smooth vertical wall and a smooth horizontal floor as shown in figure. At this moment, kinetic energy of rod is (the rod makes 45° with the floor and its lower end moves along the floor with speed V 0 ) (a) mv 0 ² (b) (1/3)mv 0 ² (c) ½mv 0 ² (d) ¼mv 0 ² —

In the figure shown a ring A is rolling without sliding with a velocity v on the horizontal surface of the body B (of same mass as A). All surfaces are smooth. B has no initial velocity. What will be the maximum height (from initial position) reached by A on B? (a) 3v²/4g (b) v²/4g (c) v²/2g (d) v²/3g —

A disc is set rolling on an inclined plane of angle 30° at its base as shown. It is in continuous rolling on plane upto height h = 1 m, then leaves the plane. If initially it had kinetic energy of 4 J, find the ratio of kinetic energy due to translation and rotation at maximum height of its trajectory (mass of disc is 0.1 kg). (a) ½ (b) 3/2 (c) ¾ (d) 2 —
